findings.text: Console keyboard interface uses distinct numeric operation identifiers. Accent table retrieval in UCS form and accent table update in UCS form use neighboring codes near the top of the range, whereas keycode table slot read and keycode table slot write use neighboring lower codes. Separately, keyboard generated signal acceptance, keyboard delay and repeat programming, and the multiplexed font operation entry each have their own fixed code.

Accent successor table for UCS input carries a count followed by a fixed capacity array of 256 diacritic combination records, each record holding three unsigned values for diacritic, base and result. Keycode table entry pairs an unsigned scancode with an unsigned keycode. Repeat control holds signed delay and period in milliseconds, where a non-positive value leaves that parameter unchanged.

Font management uses two parallel record shapes. Both carry width, height, character count and a byte pointer to glyph data. The user-facing operation form adds an operation selector plus flags and marks its data pointer as coming from user address space. The in-kernel form omits selector and flags.

Font operation selector defines set as zero and get as one, with default-font selection as two, a retired copy value as three that must not be used, plus tall variants for set and get as four and five. One flag bit requests that hardware character cell recalculation be skipped for compatibility.

First group of page state bit positions runs from zero upward through ten. In header order these denote locked, then an error slot now unused, then referenced, uptodate, dirty, least-recently-used membership, active membership, slab ownership, writeback in progress, reclaim in progress, and buddy allocator membership.

Second group of page state bit positions runs from eleven through twenty. In header order these denote mapped, anonymous, swap cache presence, swap backing, compound head, compound tail, huge page, unevictable, hardware poisoned, and no-page conditions.

Third group of page state bit positions runs from twenty-one through twenty-six. In header order these denote same-page merging, transparent huge page, offline, zero page, idle, and page table ownership.

Kernel loading control word reserves low bits for behavior selection and high sixteen bits for architecture selection. Low selections include crash kernel loading, context preservation across transition, ELF core header refresh, and crash hotplug support. A mask isolates the architecture field.

File based kernel loading uses low flag bits for unload, crash loading, omission of initial ram filesystem, debug enablement, omission of contiguous allocation, and forced device tree blob. A separate limit caps the number of loadable segments at sixteen.

Architecture selectors occupy the high sixteen bits by left shifting a small architecture number. The fragments define default plus common families including x86 in both widths, 68K, parisc, power in both widths, ia64, arm in both widths, s390, superh, both mips endian forms, riscv and loongarch.

Loadable segment descriptor holds four fields in order: source buffer address, source byte length, destination memory address, and destination memory length. Addresses are read-only pointers while lengths use the kernel address width type.

Modifier state indexes assign shift zero, altgraph one, control two, alt three, left shift four shared with kana shift, right shift five, left control six, right control seven, and caps shift eight, with nine total shift states. Key universe limits are 256 keys, at most 256 keymaps, at most 256 user keymaps, at most 256 function strings, and at most 256 diacritic entries.

Key action encoding packs a four bit type in the upper byte and an eight bit value in the lower byte, with helpers to extract each half. Type numbers run zero through fifteen for latin, function, special, pad, dead, console, cursor, shift, meta, ascii, lock, letter, sticky lock, second dead, braille and CSI with modifier support. Latin must remain zero.

Function family spans all 256 values of its type, covering numbered function actions plus editing and control helpers and ending with an undo action at the top value. Special family covers hole, enter, register and memory and status display, break, console selection, caps and num toggles, hold, scroll directions, boot, caps display, compose, secure attention, console cycling and spawn, bare numlock, plus dynamically allocated and no-such-map sentinels.

Pad family provides twenty entries for digits zero through nine plus arithmetic, enter, comma, dot, plus-minus and parenthesis helpers. Dead accent family provides twenty-seven entries for grave through greek diacritics. Cursor family provides four directional entries. Shift family derives its value from the modifier index, and ascii family provides twenty-six entries for decimal digits plus hexadecimal digits.

Lock and sticky lock families each derive values from modifier indexes and provide nine entries. Braille family provides eleven entries from blank through ten dot patterns. CSI family maps selected numeric parameters to home, insert, delete, end, paging and twenty function actions matching terminal escape suffixes.

Glyph payload pitch is fixed at thirty-two bytes per row for the normal set and get operations, while the tall variants size the pitch from the font height. Repeat programming returns the effective values in use. One historic repeat field name was inaccurate. One page flag slot is documented as no longer used.

Callers must not use the retired font copy selector, must distinguish the user pointer operation form from the kernel pointer font form, and must respect fixed capacities of the diacritic array, keymap dimensions, function string table and pad, dead, ascii, lock and braille counts.
